citation.title: Diverse Topology Optimization using Modulated Neural Fields
citation.authors: Andreas Radler, Eric Volkmann, Johannes Brandstetter, Arturs Berzins

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: On the cantilever benchmark, TOM reduces wall-clock time relative to the classical deflated-barrier method while producing diverse, near-optimal designs.
claim.key_phrase: more diverse and faster than DB
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Table 1 reports 123 min for deflated barrier and 29 min for TOM on the cantilever benchmark; 123 / 29 = 4.24. TOM uses parallel solver calls while DB is sequential (Sections 3.1, 4.4).
claim.alternatives: Table 1 reports TOM at 47 min versus FeniTop at 187 min on the jet-engine bracket; Section 4.4 states DB has better compliance than TOM, while TOM is faster and more diverse.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP/FeniTop single-solution baseline and deflated-barrier (DB) method for multiple solutions
baseline.implementation: FeniTop Python wrapper of FEniCSx/DolfinX FEM solvers; DB implementation cited to Papadopoulos et al. (2021) (Section 4.2)
baseline.solver: Finite-element solver; precise linear solver not stated
baseline.hardware_classical: Experiments run on one NVIDIA Titan V12 GPU node with Xeon Gold 6150 CPU (36 cores, 2.70 GHz) and 384 GB RAM (Appendix A.3); method-specific hardware allocation not stated
baseline.hardware_ml: Same stated node; TOM diversity computations use GPU and FEM solves are parallelized across CPU cores (Section 3.1; Appendix A.3)
baseline.classical_iterations: FeniTop 400 iterations on MBB and cantilever, 1,000 on bracket; DB 400 on MBB and cantilever (Table 2)
baseline.classical_time: DB: 123 min on cantilever; FeniTop: 187 min on jet-engine bracket (Table 1)
baseline.ml_time: TOM: 29 min on cantilever and 47 min on jet-engine bracket (Table 1); 6.1 min on MBB (Table 1)
baseline.training_time: Per-problem solver-in-the-loop optimization; TOM uses 1,000 iterations on cantilever and 400 on MBB and bracket (Table 2); no offline training time stated
baseline.data_generation_cost: No offline dataset; method described as data-free (abstract and Section 4.4)
baseline.quality_metric: Compliance, volume fraction, load-violation ratio (LVR), and Wasserstein-1 diversity (Table 1)
baseline.quality_gap: DB has better compliance: MBB TOM 0.75±0.03 vs DB 0.67±0.01; cantilever TOM 0.69±0.13 vs DB 0.58±0.01 (Table 1).

R1.evidence: Section 4.4 says DB has better compliance while TOM is faster; Table 1 reports those outcomes without matching design quality or time. TOM also uses parallel solver calls whereas DB is sequential (Sections 3.1 and 4.4).

R2.evidence: Sections 3.1 and 4.2 describe the FEM-based FeniTop baseline and parallel CPU/GPU execution; no text establishes an inefficient solver, excessive iterations, unjustified GPU-vs-CPU comparison, or a weak abstract baseline.

R3.evidence: Sections 3.1 and 4.4 describe per-problem solver-in-the-loop optimization and state TOM is data-free; there is no offline training or data-generation cost to amortize.

R4.evidence: Sections 3.1 and 4.4 evaluate compliance and volume with FEM and report load-violation ratios; Table 1 gives LVR for methods and Appendix D.3 describes removal of floaters and optional classical fine-tuning.

reporting.n_test_cases: Three benchmark problems (MBB, cantilever, jet-engine bracket); finite sample counts by method are in Table 1. TOM generates a continuous distribution that can be sampled (Table 1 caption).

notes: Table 1 reports mean and standard-deviation results and load-violation ratios. Appendix D.3 notes that optional classical fine-tuning uses 5% of a full run; timing of this post-processing is not separately reported. Public code URL is stated in the paper: https://github.com/ml-jku/Topology-Optimization-Modulated-Neural-Fields.
